text: The road ran the wrong direction—away from Uruk, away from the ridge, toward nothing they recognized. Beside it, pressed into the sand, were footprints. Bare feet. One set. Fresh.
speaker: Narrator

text: The prints started beside the buried road and led toward the ridge. Zik followed them until they stopped. No second set. No drag marks. No struggle. Only a strip of faded cloth half-buried where the last footprint ended.
speaker: Narrator

text: He knew it before he touched it. The weave. The dye gone the color of old rust. The ghost of smoke and myrrh still clinging to the fibers after twelve years of desert wind that should have scoured it clean.
speaker: Narrator

text: He picked it up. For one long moment the desert dropped away and he was eleven years old again, huddled beside a dying fire while his father draped this same cloth over his shoulders.
speaker: Narrator

text: Desert remembers the sun. Doesn't mean it owes you warmth after dark.
